#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""patch.py <contract: EZ|R|X> <tree> : the shadow patches of the integer power, as exact-text
edits that each must match once in the tree's library sources."""
import sys
C, T = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
FL, FLI = T + '/Library/FortressLibrary.fss', T + '/Library/FortressLibrary.fsi'
FB, FBI = T + '/ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss', T + '/ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi'
P = 'com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.'
edits = []
def e(f, old, new): edits.append((f, old, new))

# Each integer type: (file, api file, type, native class, header line that starts its trait in the component).
TYPES = [(FL, FLI, 'ZZ32', 'Int'), (FL, FLI, 'ZZ64', 'Long'), (FL, FLI, 'NN64', 'UnsignedLong'),
         (FL, FLI, 'ZZ', 'BigNum'), (FB, FBI, 'NN32', 'NN32')]

QQ_OLD = """    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral):QQ =
        if -other > 0 then   (* Way too clever by half (to avoid infinite recursion on 2^(-63)) *)
            (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-other)
        else
            (numerator(self))^other / (denominator(self))^other
        end
"""
# EZ: the exponent's sign split inside each of AnyIntegral's comprised types (exactValue's device).
QQ_EZ = """    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral):QQ =
        typecase other of
            e: NN32 => (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e
            e: NN64 => (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e
            e: ZZ32 => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-(widen(e))) else (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e end
            e: ZZ64 => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-e) else (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e end
            e: ZZ => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-e) else (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e end
        end
"""
# R and X: the same split, every integer power at an unsigned exponent.
QQ_RX = """    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral):QQ =
        typecase other of
            e: NN32 => (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e
            e: NN64 => (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e
            e: ZZ32 => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(unsigned(-(widen(e)))) else (numerator(self))^(unsigned(e)) / (denominator(self))^(unsigned(e)) end
            e: ZZ64 => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(unsigned(-e)) else (numerator(self))^(unsigned(e)) / (denominator(self))^(unsigned(e)) end
            e: ZZ => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(unsigned(-(widen(e)))) else (numerator(self))^(unsigned(widen(e))) / (denominator(self))^(unsigned(widen(e))) end
        end
"""

if C == 'EZ':
    e(FL, "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr |\self/|: I = self", "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):I
    opr |\self/|: I = self")
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):I
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):I
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):I
")
    for (f, fi, t, n) in TYPES:
        e(f, '    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%s%s$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64 = self^(b.asZZ32)' % (P, n),
             '    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):%s =
        builtinPrimitive("%s%s$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):%s = self^(b.asZZ32)' % (t, P, n, t))
    e(FB, '    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%sIntLiteral$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): RR64 = self^(b.asZZ32)' % P,
          '    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):IntLiteral =
        builtinPrimitive("%sIntLiteral$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): IntLiteral = self^(b.asZZ32)' % P)
    # the api
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):NN64
")
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ32
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ32
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ32
")
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ64
")
    e(FLI, "    opr /(self,other:ZZ):QQ
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr /(self,other:ZZ):QQ
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ
")
    e(FBI, "    opr BITNOT(self):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):NN32
")
    e(FBI, "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): RR64
", "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):IntLiteral
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): IntLiteral
")
    e(FL, QQ_OLD, QQ_EZ)
elif C in ('R', 'X'):
    # the ring's power takes a natural exponent; the fields keep their own integer exponent
    e(FL, "    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral): T
end", "    opr ^(self, other:NN64): T
end")
    e(FLI, "    opr ^(self, other:ZZ64): T
", "    opr ^(self, other:NN64): T
")
    e(FL, "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr |\self/|: I = self", "    opr |\self/|: I = self")
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):I
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):I
")
    def signed(t):
        if C != 'R': return ''
        return ('
    opr ^(self, b:ZZ32):QQ = do q: QQ = self; q^b end'
                '
    opr ^(self, b:ZZ64):QQ = do q: QQ = self; q^b end'
                '
    opr ^(self, b:ZZ):QQ = do q: QQ = self; q^b end')
    def signedApi():
        if C != 'R': return ''
        return '    opr ^(self, b:ZZ32):QQ
    opr ^(self, b:ZZ64):QQ
    opr ^(self, b:ZZ):QQ
'
    for (f, fi, t, n) in TYPES:
        e(f, '    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%s%s$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64 = self^(b.asZZ32)' % (P, n),
             '    opr ^(self, b:NN64):%s =
        builtinPrimitive("%s%s$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):%s =
        builtinPrimitive("%s%s$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):%s = self^(b.asNN64)%s' % (t, P, n, t, P, n, t, signed(t)))
    e(FB, '    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%sIntLiteral$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): RR64 = self^(b.asZZ32)' % P,
          '    opr ^(self, b:NN64):IntLiteral =
        builtinPrimitive("%sIntLiteral$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):IntLiteral =
        builtinPrimitive("%sIntLiteral$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): IntLiteral = self^(b.asNN64)%s' % (P, P, signed('IntLiteral')))
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):NN64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):NN64
" + signedApi())
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ32
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ32
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):ZZ32
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):ZZ32
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ32
" + signedApi())
    e(FLI, "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):ZZ64
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):ZZ64
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):ZZ64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ64
" + signedApi())
    e(FLI, "    opr /(self,other:ZZ):QQ
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr /(self,other:ZZ):QQ
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):ZZ
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):ZZ
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ
" + signedApi())
    e(FBI, "    opr BITNOT(self):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):RR64
", "    opr BITNOT(self):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):NN32
    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):NN32
" + signedApi())
    e(FBI, "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): RR64
", "    opr ^(self, b:NN64):IntLiteral
    opr ^(self, b:NN32):IntLiteral
    opr ^(self, b: IntLiteral): IntLiteral
" + signedApi())
    e(FL, QQ_OLD, QQ_RX)
    # walk's abstract-method check takes a body only at or below the ring's NN64 exponent, so each
    # other ring object gets one (Float, FloatLiteral, RR32, QQ's Ratio through QQ)
    e(FB, "    (** Shouldn't need this extra declaration. **)
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%sFloat$Pow")" % P,
          "    (** Shouldn't need this extra declaration. **)
    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%sFloat$Pow")
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):RR64 =
        builtinPrimitive("%sFloat$Pow")" % (P, P))
    e(FB, "FloatLiteral$AsFloat")
", "FloatLiteral$AsFloat")
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):RR64 = (asFloat(self))^b
")
    e(FB, "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR32 = narrow((asFloat(self))^b)
", "    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR32 = narrow((asFloat(self))^b)
    opr ^(self, b:NN64):RR32 = narrow((asFloat(self))^b)
")
    e(FL, "    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral):QQ =
        typecase other of", "    opr ^(self, other:NN64):QQ = (numerator(self))^other / (denominator(self))^other
    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral):QQ =
        typecase other of")
    if C == 'X':
        # the library's callers with a signed exponent, converted
        e(FL, "d radix^(n-i)", "d radix^(unsigned(n-i))")
        e(FL, "10^k (both[|both| - 1 - k].codePoint - '0'.codePoint))/(10^(|frac|)))",
              "10^(unsigned(k)) (both[|both| - 1 - k].codePoint - '0'.codePoint))/(10^(unsigned(|frac|))))")
else:
    sys.exit('unknown contract ' + C)

texts = {}
for (f, old, new) in edits:
    s = texts.get(f) or open(f).read()
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != 1: sys.exit('edit matches %d times in %s:
%s' % (n, f, old))
    texts[f] = s.replace(old, new)
for f, s in texts.items(): open(f, 'w').write(s)
print('%s: %d edits in %d files' % (C, len(edits), len(texts)))

content.content:
## 1. What changed

The branch was new; nothing was inherited. Four commits: the tests alone (`62a62f94c`, `8166315d4`), the edit (`91ed5d776`), and a follow-up the first distance run asked for (`e995c31c0`). Under Q1 = (a) the rung repaired the Meet Rule pairs one type provides, String's own juxtaposition pair and the declared-type slips, and left every top-level pair of two functional methods to rung O.

**Meet Rule pairs, declarations on the meet (P2's devices M and C, and three more):**
- `Maybe` declares `map[\G\](f: T->G): Maybe[\G\]` and `ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,T)->G): Maybe[\G\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:920-921; the component's bodies at Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1441-1444, `cond` over `Just` and `Nothing` as `Condition`'s bodies do). In the api `Maybe` is the first type below both `Condition` and `ZeroIndexed` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:917).
- `StandardMutableArrayType` declares `copy():T` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1466, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2134), abstract, where `fill` and `tabulate` already meet.
- `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` declares `map`, answering a `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` over the composed function (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3554-3555); `SimpleNestedSeqGenerator` declares `map`, answering a `SimpleNestedSeqGenerator` that maps each inner sequential generator, and `nest`, `NestedGenerator`'s body restated (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3635-3638). The precedent is `SimpleSeqFilterGenerator`'s own `seq` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3584).
- `String`'s juxtaposition: the three functional methods of `String` (`(a:Any, self)`, `(self, b:String)`, `(self, b:Any)`) become three top-level operators with the same bodies (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2440-2443, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4237-4240). Two functional methods with `self` at different positions satisfy neither the Subtype nor the Incompatibility Rule, and the text admits no meet for them (Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:517-523); as top-level functions the Meet Rule for functions is met by `(String, String)` (:411-415 contrasts the two rules).

**Slips, each declared type set to what its body answers (P2's S and the rest):**
- the api's `AssociativeReduction.lift(r:R)` against `ActualReduction.lift(r:R)` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1860); the component's `lift(r:Any)` throughout is unchanged.
- the api's `LessThan` and `GreaterThan` `CMP(self, other: LessThan|GreaterThan): TotalComparison`, as the component already declares (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:139, :150).
- `LeftScalarRange.every: BoundedScalarRange`, `LeftScalarRange.atMost` and `RightScalarRange.atMost: FullScalarRange` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:240, :242, :298; Library/RangeInternals.fss:563, :571, :683), and `RightScalarRange.every: BoundedScalarRange` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:296, Library/RangeInternals.fss:675), whose body answers a `LeftScalarRange` for a negative stride.
- `FilterGenerator.filter: FilterGenerator[\E\]`, the api's own type (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3568 against Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2101); `MappedGenerator.map: MappedGenerator[\E,G\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3517). Each had declared an object type that the override in `FilterGenerator2` and `SimpleMappedIndexed` could not answer.
- `ConcreteRelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]` extends `RelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]`, not `[\()\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4598); its `relation` and `target` then answer its parent's.
- `SimpleNestedGenerator.seq: SequentialGenerator[\F\]` and `SimplePairGenerator.seq: SequentialGenerator[\(E,F)\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3617, :3659).
- `Array3.shift: Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1777, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2881); `Col` and `Row`'s `subarray: Array1[\T,b,s\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2626, :2637). No code constructs a `Col` or a `Row`, so no walk program reaches the last two.
- `EmptyString` and `FlatString`'s `split(): Generator[\String\] = Nothing[\String\]` and `splitWithOffsets(): Generator[\(ZZ32,String)\] = Nothing[\(ZZ32,String)\]` (Library/String.fss:317-318, Library/FlatString.fss:146-147), the empty generator the api's comment asks for (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2382-2390). This is row 356.
- the unary `BIG MAX` returns `T` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3247; row 472), and the nullary `BIG MINMAX` is a `Comprehension[\T,(T,T),(T,T),AnyMaybe\]`, as `BIG MIN_MIN`'s siblings are (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1951, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3259-3260; row 473).
- row 483: `UniformDistribution[\T\](range: FullRange[\T\])` (Library/Random.fsi:258, Library/Random.fss:370), so `T` is the range's element type and a `ZZ64` distribution over a `ZZ32` range is refused at construction.
- row 531: `getter avFlat(): RR32 = narrow(asFloat(ssize) / asFloat(numFlat))` (Library/String.fss:508).

**Tests.** New in `ProjectFortress/tests/`: `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` (every repaired declaration a program can reach, called with the value it answers, passing before and after, and two values pinned as today's), `BigMinMax.fss`, `SequentialGeneratorMap.fss`, `XXXUniformDistributionRangeType.fss`. Promoted by `git mv`, component renamed, no assertion changed: `XXXStringAvFlatRungV.fss` to `StringAvFlat.fss` (row 531), `XXXFlatStringSplitRungL.fss` to `FlatStringSplit.fss` (row 356, which the split repair turns green). Review-routed.2: `XXXComprisesMeetUncovered.fss` to `XXXComprisesMeetUncoveredWalk.fss` with its component. Review-routed.1: the messages of `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ComprisesMeetCompiled.fss:18` and `ProjectFortress/tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss:18` now say that by the comprises clauses of S and T and U's excludes clause every value of both S and T is a value of V, so V covers their intersection (Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:367-372); the ledger row number left the message, as the register asks; the assertions are unchanged.

## 4. Each device, with the ways not taken

- **`Maybe`'s `map` and `ivmap`, P2's M.** Not taken: making the api's `Condition` extend `ZeroIndexed` as its component does (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1330 against Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:854), with the api's `ivmap` answering a `Condition` as the component's does, which would make `Condition` the meet in the api too. It is batch 7b's precedent of an api matching its component, but it changes the api parents of every `Condition`, `Boolean` among them, and needs more api declarations retyped; the meet declaration is the smaller device and the one P2 measured.
- **`copy` on `StandardMutableArrayType`, P2's C.** Not taken: redeclaring `copy` in each array leaf, the library's way for `copy` until now, which FACTS ("fill takes a value and tabulate a function, both defined where the array diamond meets") records leaves the meet refused.
- **`map` and `nest` on the two sequential generators.** For `map` there is no other way: `SequentialGenerator.map` declares a `SequentialGenerator` result (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:846), so any declaration on the meet answers one. For `nest` both parents answer a `Generator`, and the declaration keeps `NestedGenerator`'s body, today's value; not taken, `SequentialGenerator.nest`'s typecase, which would make some results sequential.
- **`String`'s juxtaposition, three top-level operators.** Not taken: (a) moving only `(a:Any, self)` to the top level, which the text accepts by the Meet Rule for functions (Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:525-528) but today's checker refuses, since its meet rule asks the three declarations' self positions to agree (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:501-523`); changing that is rung O's stop (row 545's family). (b) narrowing `(a:Any, self)` to a type that excludes `String`, which would refuse `x "text"` for every other `x` and change what the library's own bodies print. The move keeps every body and every value; walk's choice is unchanged in the 38 tests run. Found on the way: the checker never checks `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///` (the fourth named at the gather, the skeptic's correction 6), whose pairs on `String` have the same shape (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2411-2412`, `:2418-2419`, `:2424-2425`, `:2430-2431` at `e995c31c0`; row 585), because `NU.validOp` does not admit those names (`OverloadingChecker.scala:567-571`); a probe declaring the same three shapes for `||`, `juxtaposition`, `DOT` and a named method reports all but `||` (section 7).
- **`cross`, no device: rung O's capture fix.** Its three messages show the method's `[\F\]` captured by the trait's `F`: "[\F\](SequentialGenerator[\F\], Generator[\F\])->Generator[\(F, F)\]" (explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:96). A three-trait probe under the compiler library reports "Invalid overloading of cross in trait MappedSeq: [\F extends Any\](SeqGen[\F\], Gen[\F\])->Gen[\(F, F)\] ... and [\G extends Any\](Gen[\F\], Gen[\G\])->Gen[\(F, G)\]", and nothing once the method's parameter is renamed `H` (section 7). Not taken: that rename in the library (the triage's device for `generate`), which would hide whether O's fix covers `cross`.

## 5. Left, each with its row

- **`LexicographicReduction.isLeftZero(_:Comparison)`, 2 M1 errors and the count's 1.** Walk answers `false` for `LessThan`, `EqualTo` and `GreaterThan` (probe line `H2 isLeftZero false false false`): the inherited `ReductionWithZeroes.isLeftZero(l: TotalComparison)` is more specific than the team's `Comparison` overload, so the team's `true` for `LessThan` and `GreaterThan` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:122-123) is never reached. P2's repair, the parameter declared `TotalComparison`, makes it reached and changes the answer to `true`; deleting the unreachable overload keeps every answer and drops the team's declaration. The section leaves a slip whose repair changes a value walk prints with a row, so neither is built; nothing in the library or the corpora calls `isLeftZero`. Pinned by `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` ("today's value"); new row, provisionally 582.
- **The full sequential ranges' `map`, 2.** `CompactFullSeqScalarRange` and `StridedFullSeqScalarRange` inherit `SequentialGenerator`'s and `Indexed`'s `map` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:418, :491); a declaration on the meet must answer a type below both, and no library type is both an `Indexed` and a `SequentialGenerator` but `Condition`. The library's precedent would be a new object at that meet, as `SimpleMappedIndexed` and `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` are for theirs, exported from the api for `RangeInternals` to name. Walk answers `SequentialGenerator`'s, sequential and not indexed (`B1 compactseq.map mapped(seq(10,11,12)) seq notindexed`). Pinned in `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss`; new row, provisionally 583.
- **`SumReduction`'s two `distribute`, 2 R3.** Each declares `PossibleReductionPair[\AnyMaybe\]` against `ActualReduction`'s `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, and its body is a `PossibleReductionPair[\AnyMaybe\]` because the component's `ReductionPair[\R,L\]` extends `SomeReductionPair[\L\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3041) where the api's extends `SomeReductionPair[\R\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1850). Declaring `[\T\]` moves the error into the body; aligning the component's parent moves it to `outer` and `inner`. The team's note says the same: "we do not have any way to capture the type L" (Library/Generator2.fss:170-172). A note on row 433, the same declarations.
- **`StandardTotalOrder.MINMAX`'s body (:290 on the base, R4 by the classifier).** The declared `(T,T)` is right; the body's `self` is a `StandardTotalOrder[\T\]`, not a `T`: the self-typed bodies of class S1 (Q2, not in this batch). A note on row 421.
- **`BIG MINMAX` with no static argument.** The repaired nullary now builds; walk binds its `T` to `BOTTOM` and `MinMaxReduction`'s `simpleJoin(a:(T,T), b:(T,T))` then accepts no element: "MethodClosure simpleJoin(a:Any,b:Any):Any ... has neither body nor def". That is row 424; a note on row 473.

## 6. The three homes

| defect | home | where |
|---|---|---|
| a sequential mapped or nested generator, mapped again, answers a non-sequential generator under walk (`D1 ... mapped(2,4,6) notseq`, `E1 ... notseq`) | 1, repaired by the meet declarations | `ProjectFortress/tests/SequentialGeneratorMap.fss` |
| `BIG MINMAX` at an explicit static argument or applied to a generator stops walk (row 473) | 1 | `ProjectFortress/tests/BigMinMax.fss` |
| `UniformDistribution[\T\]` answers `ZZ32` values as any `T` (row 483) | 1, refused | `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXUniformDistributionRangeType.fss` (must fail, as rung W's walk controls) |
| `avFlat` (row 531), `split` (row 356) | 1 | `StringAvFlat.fss`, `FlatStringSplit.fss`, promoted |
| `isLeftZero` unreachable for a total comparison | 3, the specification does not define `isLeftZero` | `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` pins `false`; row 582 (provisional) |
| the full sequential ranges' `map` | 3: the text settles that the pair needs a declaration on the meet, the checker refuses it rightly, and the library has no type to declare it at | `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` pins the mapped elements; row 583 (provisional) |
| `BIG MINMAX` with no static argument | row 424's | note on row 473 |
| `UniformDistribution`'s `min(g)` without a written static argument fails under walk ("RandomGen[\T@...\] got arg LinearCongruential[\ZZ64\]") | row 21's (a method's static argument is not inferred) | the walk test writes `min[\ZZ64\]` |
| `cross`'s capture | rung O's capture fix | section 4 |
| `UniformDistribution`'s `min` and `max` over a strided range stop walk, "Cannot find definition for method lower given receiver StridedFullParScalarRange" (`Library/Random.fss:373`), on the base and the edit (the skeptic's `SkUniformStrided`; added at the gather) | 2 | `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXUniformDistributionStridedRange.fss`, asserting `Just(2)` and `Just(8)` for `UniformDistribution[\ZZ32\](2:8:3)`, an expected failure through `harness-one.sh` ("OK Saw expected exception") and failing on a stand-in over `2:8` ("Missing expected failure"); row 586 |
| the compiled overloading checker skips every symbolic operator, so `opr +(x:A, y:A)` beside `opr +(x:B, y:B)` over two unrelated traits passes (the skeptic's `SkOpBlind`, which reports only `MYOP` and `f`; added at the gather) | the row alone, row 584: an expected-failure compile test cannot hold an over-acceptance; the gather wrote `XXXOperatorOverloadNoMeet.fss` with `compile_err_contains=Invalid overloading of +` as the skeptic asked and the harness failed it on the batch's merged tree, "Saw failure, but did not satisfy compile_err_contains", "Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1", the compile having succeeded (`FileTests.java:383-399`), so it is not landed | row 584 |
| `String`'s `\|\|`, `\|\|\|`, `//` and `///` each pair `(a:Any, self)` with `(self, b:Any)`, the shape the specification refuses (added at the gather) | the row alone, row 585, while the checker skips symbolic operators | row 585 |

## 7. Probes and differentials

All under `tmp/rung-library-meets/probes/`, not committed. `MeetProbe.fss` under walk on the base and on the edit (`bin/fortress MeetProbe.fss`): 33 lines, identical but `D1` and `E1` (the two maps now sequential, the same elements in the same order) and the last, `BIG MINMAX[x <- 0#4] x`, which moves from the `Comprehension` refusal to the `simpleJoin` failure of row 424:

    < D1 mappedseq.map mapped(2,4,6) notseq 2,4,6,
    > D1 mappedseq.map mapped(seq(2,4,6)) seq 2,4,6,
    < E1 nestedseq.map seq(0,1).nest(f) notseq 1,2,11,12,
    > E1 nestedseq.map seq(seq(0,1).nest(f)) seq 1,2,11,12,

The final tree prints the same as the first edit. `MeetProbe2.fss` (split, `shift`, the relational predicate, `filter`, `map` on mapped generators) prints the same values on base and edit. `EveryProbe.fss` prints the same five range renderings on the base library and the edit. `juxt/JuxtProbe.fss` (`fortress typecheck -compiler-lib`): `Invalid overloading of juxtaposition in trait S`, of `DOT`, of `foo`, and nothing for `||`. `capture/CrossCapture.fss` and `CrossRenamed.fss` (`fortress typecheck -compiler-lib`): the capture message above, then no error.

## 8. Precedent search

The team's way for a method two parents provide is a declaration in the type below both: `SimpleSeqFilterGenerator`'s `seq` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3584), `SimpleMappedIndexed`'s `map` (:3544), the array diamond's `fill` and `tabulate` (:2126-2133; FACTS, "fill takes a value and tabulate a function, both defined where the array diamond meets"). Three of this rung's meet declarations copy that shape; `Maybe`'s and `copy`'s are P2's. The record's other devices, plain exclusion traits (`Rank1` to `Rank3`, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1156-1166) and markers, are for top-level pairs, which under Q1 = (a) are rung O's; no device here states an exclusion. For a slip the precedent is batch 7's row 421 (`MIN` and `MAX` declared as their bodies return) and row 531's `narrow`. # skip-patch.py <shadow StaticChecker.java>: under -Dprobe.skipBodies=true, the tolerant

If the \KWD{comprises} clause of a trait \VAR{T} includes ``\EXP{\ldots}''
(and must therefore be in an API),

other traits may explicitly extend \VAR{T},

A trait declaration of \VAR{T} that has no \KWD{comprises} clause,
or one that lists no type but ``\EXP{\ldots}'', may have a \emph{self-type parameter}:
a static parameter \VAR{X} of \VAR{T}
whose bounds include \VAR{T} at its own static parameters,
as in \EXP{\KWD{trait}\;T\llbracket{}X \KWD{extends} T\llbracket{}X\rrbracket\rrbracket},
or include an instantiation of a trait with a self-type parameter
that \VAR{T} also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause,
with \VAR{X} as the static argument for that self-type parameter.
In the bodies of the methods of \VAR{T},
\KWD{self} then has the type \EXP{T \cap X} (\secref{idn-ref}).
A trait or object declaration, or an object expression,
that extends an instantiation of \VAR{T}
must be a subtype of the static argument of that instantiation
for the self-type parameter of \VAR{T}; for a trait declaration the requirement is on
the type of \KWD{self} in the bodies of its methods (\secref{idn-ref}), the intersection of its type
with the types its \KWD{comprises} clause lists, or with its own self-type parameter \VAR{Y}.
It is a static error otherwise.
An object declaration has no self-type parameter.

%(* Not allowed! *)

The library's scalar extension generalised and its exclusion tower closed

Four sites in Library/FortressLibrary.fss, mirrored in .fsi:

- :4496-4504 (api :2540-2547), the block that was :4493-4517: the integer scalar-extension block
  `opr + - MIN MAX (Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\], ZZ32)` becomes eight generic
  declarations `[\T extends Number, I\]`, both operand orders, on the
  precedent of the `T extends Number` array operators at :2264-2279 and
  :2624-2637.
- :612 (api :409): `trait AnyIntegral extends { QQ } comprises { ZZ }`
  closes the numeric tower's one open comprises link; the api already
  closes `ZZ` at :536.
- :327-328 (api :250-251): the `AnyMultiplicativeRing` placeholder pattern
  of :338-339 (api :262-263) applied to `AdditiveGroup` -- a marker `trait
  AnyAdditiveGroup end` that `AdditiveGroup` extends.
- :2669 (api :1659): `Array3 excludes { Number, String, AnyAdditiveGroup,
  AnyMultiplicativeRing }`.

Why the tower has to be closed for the generic block to load beside
`AdditiveGroup.+` and `StandardTotalOrder.MAX`: the interpreter makes a
trait with a `comprises` clause exclude whatever every leaf of its
transitive comprises excludes (FType.java:281-297,
FTypeTrait.java:68-78). `ZZ32`'s leaves are the objects `Int` and
`IntLiteral`, which is why the shipped ground block loads; `RR64`'s leaves
included `AnyIntegral`, a trait with no comprises clause, which excludes
nothing, so nothing above `RR64` excluded the symbolic bound of a library
operator's type variable and the generic block over `T extends Number`
would be refused. With `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ }` the tower is closed.
The marker trait and the `Array3` clause do the same for a user operator
whose non-self operand is an `Array3`.

The two tests, each run from an empty FORTRESS_CACHES, red on the tree
before this edit and green after:

- tests/ArrayScalarExtension.fss -- 24 checks of `+ - MIN MAX` in both
  operand orders over an `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, a `Matrix` and an
  `Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]`, the last pinning the shipped block's behaviour,
  which no test asserted. Before: "Failed to find any matching overload,
  args = (__DefaultVector[\RR64,3\],1.0)".

# make.py WAY OUTDIR: writes patched copies of the three library files for one way of probe P2.
#   J   juxtaposition's device on ||, |||, // and ///: each family's (a:Any, self), (self, b:String)
#       and (self, b:Any) become three top-level operators; bodies as they were (a.asString stays)
#   JC  J, and the bodies turn any value into a string by the library's own ways:
#       ("" || a) on the left, as juxtaposition's (a:Any, b:String) does, and cast[\Object\] at the bottom
#   JCp JC with the meet's body concatAndBalanceIfNecessary (the first form measured): walk then runs
#       that body for every concatenation of two strings, since no program sees the string objects' own ||
#   JH  the hook kept: String keeps its abstract opr ||(self, b:String), through which every program reaches
#       the string objects' own ||; the other two || members and the other three families as in JC
#   C   the conversion alone: String's functional methods kept, their two bodies as in JC

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fix.py <tree> <family>...: the sorting probe's library patches, as exact-text edits that must
each match once.  Families:
  flat     FlatString's api pair (row 726): drop opr ||(a:FlatString, self), which the component lacks
  empty    EmptyString's || (row 611): the meet opr ||(self, _:EmptyString) in the component, and in
           String's api too when str4 is applied (str4 makes EmptyString's members visible there)
  str4     String's four concatenation families (row 585): juxtaposition's device, the earlier probe's
           way J (three top-level operators per family, bodies as they were, String api's 5 lines)
  eq       = : Integral's meet opr =(self, b:I) (api and component, bodiless as Integral's others),
           and ZZ's api opr =(self, b:ZZ), which its component declares
  abs      |_| : Maybe's api meet, SubString's api declaration its component has, Float's |self|: RR64
  maybeidx Maybe's api subscript meet opr[i:ZZ32]: T
  vecops   the api's six top-level Vector and Matrix + and -, which the component does not define
  pow      the integer power (a design choice): probe P1's E/Z library text, row 445's AnyIntegral
           exponent in the api, Float's meet opr ^(self, b:RR64)
"""
import sys, subprocess
T = sys.argv[1]; fams = sys.argv[2:]
FL, FLI = T + '/Library/FortressLibrary.fss', T + '/Library/FortressLibrary.fsi'
FB, FBI = T + '/ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss', T + '/ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi'
SS, SSI, FSI = T + '/Library/String.fss', T + '/Library/String.fsi', T + '/Library/FlatString.fsi'
edits = []
def e(f, old, new): edits.append((f, old, new))

if 'flat' in fams:
    e(FSI, "    opr ||(a:FlatString, self): String\n", "")

if 'empty' in fams:
    e(SS, "    opr || (self, other:String): String = other\n    opr || (self, other:Char):String = other.asString\n",
          "    opr || (self, other:String): String = other\n    opr || (self, _:EmptyString): String = self\n    opr || (self, other:Char):String = other.asString\n")

if 'str4' in fams:
    # component: String's members out
    e(FL, "    opr ||(self, b:String):String\n    opr ||(self, b:Number)", "    opr ||(self, b:Number)")
    e(FL, "    opr ||(a:Any, self):String = a.asString || self\n    opr ||(self, b:Any):String = self || b.asString\n", "")
    e(FL, """    opr |||(self, b:String): String =
        if |self| = 0 then b
        elif |b| = 0 then self
        else self || " " || b
        end
    opr |||(self, b:Any): String = self ||| (""||b)
    opr |||(a:Any, self): String = (""||a) ||| self
""", "")
    e(FL, """    opr //(self, a:String): String = self || newline || a
    opr //(self, a:Any): String    = self || newline || a
    opr //(a:Any, self): String    = a || newline || self
""", "")
    e(FL, """    opr ///(self, a:String): String = self || doubleNewline || a
    opr ///(self, a:Any): String    = self || doubleNewline || a

opr ||(a:String, b:Any):String

opr |||(a:String, b:String):String

opr //(a:Any, b:String):String
opr //(a:String, b:String):String
opr //(a:String, b:Any):String
opr ///(a:Any, b:String):String
opr ///(a:String, b:String):String
opr ///(a:String, b:Any):String

(** Right now for backward compatibility juxtaposition works like %||% **)

    e(FL, "    opr -(self):I\n    opr DOTMINUS(self):I\n    opr +(self,b:I):I\n",
          "    opr -(self):I\n    opr DOTMINUS(self):I\n    opr =(self,b:I):Boolean\n    opr +(self,b:I):I\n")
    e(FLI, "    coerce(x: IntLiteral)\n    opr <(self, other:ZZ): Boolean\n",

    e(FLI, "    opr SQCAP(self, o: Maybe[\\T\\]): Maybe[\\T\\]\n    map[\\G\\](f: T->G): Maybe[\\G\\]\n",

           way J (three top-level operators per family, bodies as they were, String api's 5 lines)

           and ZZ's api opr =(self, b:ZZ), which its component declares

  maybeidx Maybe's api subscript meet opr[i:ZZ32]: T

  -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "${SHADOW_CP:+$SHADOW_CP:}$(../bin/fortress_classpath|tail -1)" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest

#!/bin/bash
# harness-one.sh <scratch-dir> <file.fss>... : rung C's harness-one.sh (explorations/compile-ladder/
# rung-interp-coercion/, itself rung I's shape): the testSystem harness (SystemJUTest, the class build.xml's
# testSystem shards run) over a directory holding only the named test files, with the JVM settings of
# build.xml's systemShard macro and a private cache. Run from FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh.
#
# The scratch directory is deleted when the call starts and when it ends. The private cache is the folder
# <scratch-dir>.cache beside it, kept between calls. A call starts from what that folder holds when it was
# filled under the implementation now built (ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp, which ant compileAll
# writes) and from the Fortress sources now on the source path outside the scratch directory (the .fss and
# .fsi files of Library, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin, ProjectFortress/test_library and ProjectFortress);
# otherwise it empties the folder first. COLD_CACHE=1 empties it in any case. The folder is stamped only when
# the JVM ends normally, so a call that is killed leaves it to be emptied by the next one.
set -u
S=$(realpath -m -- "${1:?scratch dir}") ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
C=$S.cache
BUILT=$FH/ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp
sources_key () {
    ( cd "$FH" && { find Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin ProjectFortress/test_library -type f -name '*.fs[si]' -print0
                    find ProjectFortress -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.fs[si]' -print0 ; } \
        | sort -z | xargs -0 -r sha1sum | sha1sum | cut -c1-40 )
}
key () { [ -f "$BUILT" ] && echo "$(head -1 "$BUILT") sources $(sources_key)" ; }
rm -rf "$S" ; mkdir -p "$S/tests" "$S/tmp"
KEY=$(key)
if [ -z "${COLD_CACHE:-}" ] && [ -n "$KEY" ] && [ "$(cat "$C/harness.stamp" 2>/dev/null)" = "$KEY" ]; then
    CACHE=filled
else
    rm -rf "$C" ; mkdir -p "$C" ; printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$C/global.map" ; CACHE=empty
fi
rm -f "$C/harness.stamp"
for f in "$@" ; do cp "$f" "$S/tests/" ; done
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
echo "# harness-one $(date -u +%FT%TZ); tree $(git -C "$FH" rev-parse --short HEAD); nproc=$(nproc); load $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=4; cache $CACHE"
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress" && FORTRESS_THREADS=4 FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1 FORTRESS_CACHES="$C" \
  java -Xmx768m -Xss32m -Djava.io.tmpdir="$S/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$C" -Dtests="$S/tests" \
       -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest 2>&1 | grep -v '^\s*at ' | sed "s#$FH/##g"
RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "exit=$RC"
# The cache is stamped only if the run ended normally and nothing it is keyed on changed meanwhile.
[ "$RC" = 0 ] && [ -n "$KEY" ] && [ "$(key)" = "$KEY" ] && echo "$KEY" > "$C/harness.stamp"
rm -rf "$S"

as predicates in an if expression. **)
trait Condition[\E\] extends { ZeroIndexed[\E\], SequentialGenerator[\E\] }
    getter isEmpty(): Boolean = NOT self.holds
    getter nonEmpty(): Boolean = NOT self.isEmpty
    getter holds(): Boolean = cond[\Boolean\](fn (_:E):Boolean => true, fn () => false)
    getter size(): ZZ32 = if self.holds then 1 else 0 end
    getter get(): E throws NotFound = cond[\E\](identity[\E\], fn () => throw NotFound)
    getter bounds(): CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self|
    getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = self.bounds
    getter indexValuePairs(): Condition[\(ZZ32,E)\] =
        cond[\Maybe[\(ZZ32,E)\]\](fn (e:E):Maybe[\(ZZ32,E)\] => Just[\(ZZ32,E)\](0,e),
                              fn ():Maybe[\(ZZ32,E)\] => Nothing[\(ZZ32,E)\])
    getter reverse() : Condition[\E\] = self
    opr |self|: ZZ32 = if self.holds then 1 else 0 end
    opr [i:ZZ32]:E throws NotFound = if i=0 then self.get else throw NotFound end
    opr [r:Range[\ZZ32\]]: Condition[\E\] =
        cond[\Condition[\E\]\](fn (e:E): Condition[\E\] => do
                    r1 = (0#1).narrowToRange(r)
                    if r1.isEmpty then Nothing[\E\] else self end
                  end,
                fn (): Condition[\E\] => do r1 = (0#0).narrowToRange(r); self end)
    getDefault(e:E): E = cond[\E\](identity[\E\], fn () => e)
    cond[\G\](t: E -> G, e: () -> G): G
    generate[\G\](r:Reduction[\G\], body: E -> G): G = cond[\G\](body,fn () => r.empty())

    (** For a Condition, these methods run eagerly. **)
    map[\G\](f: E->G): Condition[\G\] =
        cond[\Maybe[\G\]\](fn (e:E):Maybe[\G\] => Just[\G\](f(e)), fn ():Maybe[\G\] => Nothing[\G\])
    ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,E)->G): Condition[\G\] =
        cond[\Maybe[\G\]\](fn (e:E):Maybe[\G\] => Just[\G\](f(0,e)), fn ():Maybe[\G\] => Nothing[\G\])

content.content:
\section{Declarations with Static Parameters}
\seclabel{overloading-static-params}

The rules above compare the parameter types and the return types of
declarations without static parameters.
A declaration with static parameters is read as one declaration whose parameter
type ranges over every instance of it whose static arguments satisfy their
bounds (\secref{overloading-terms}).
A declaration $d_1$ is more specific than a declaration $d_2$ when $d_2$ is
applicable to every call to which $d_1$ is applicable, and not the other way
round (\secref{resolving-overloading}); where neither has static parameters,
this is the relation $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$ of the rules above.
A set of overloaded declarations, some or all of which have static parameters,
is a valid overloading when every pair $d_1$, $d_2$ of them satisfies the
following three rules:
\begin{itemize}
\item
The \emph{No Duplicates Rule}: $d_1$ and $d_2$ are not each applicable to every
call to which the other is applicable.
\item
The \emph{Meet Rule}: $d_1$ and $d_2$ exclude each other, or one of them is more
specific than the other, or some declaration of the set is more specific than
both and applicable to every call to which both are applicable.
\item
The \emph{Return Type Rule}: if $d_1$ is more specific than $d_2$, then for
every argument type other than \TYP{BottomType} to which $d_1$ is applicable,
and for every instance of $d_2$ that is applicable to it, some instance of $d_1$
is applicable to it whose return type is a subtype of the return type of that
instance of $d_2$.
\end{itemize}
\revision{revival-overloading}{The revival's text of 30~September 2026 stated
the No Duplicates Rule as ``$d_1$ and $d_2$ are not each more specific than the
other'', which the strict sense of more specific above made refuse no pair.
It is stated on the relation without ``and not the other way round'', as the
type group's papers of 2011 and 2019 state it, and so it refuses
\EXP{\VAR{dup}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket(x\COLON \TYP{Box}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket)}
beside \EXP{\VAR{dup}\llbracket{}U\rrbracket(x\COLON
\TYP{Box}\llbracket{}U\rrbracket)}, each applicable to every call to which the
other is.}
The Subtype Rule, the Incompatibility Rule and the Meet Rule above are these
rules for declarations without static parameters, with the conditions that
coercion adds; the Return Type Rule is the Subtype Rule's condition on return
types, checked over every instance of the less specific declaration and not
over one instance chosen for the pair.

As in \secref{more-specific-rule}, declarations of the set that are each more
specific than both $d_1$ and $d_2$ and that together cover every argument to
which both are applicable also satisfy the Meet Rule.
\revision{revival-meet}{The type group's paper of 2011 states the Meet Rule
without this case.}

Two parameter types with static parameters exclude each other, for the Meet
Rule and the Incompatibility Rule, as the type group's paper of 2011 decides it
by \emph{existential reduction}: each static parameter stands for any type
within its bound, and where the two parameter types mention one parameterized
trait, instantiation exclusion (\secref{trait-types}) lets them meet only where
the static arguments of those mentions are the same, every static argument but
an operator argument counting.
So where \TYP{Box} and \TYP{Pair} are distinct object types with static
parameters, the parameter types \EXP{\TYP{Box}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket} and
\EXP{\TYP{Pair}\llbracket{}A, B\rrbracket} of two declarations exclude each
other whatever \VAR{T}, \VAR{A} and \VAR{B} stand for.

The Return Type Rule refuses the following pair, where trait \TYP{Round}
extends trait \TYP{Shape} and object \TYP{Circle} extends \TYP{Round}:
%(* Not allowed! *)
%ident[\T extends Shape\](x: T): T = x
%ident(x: Round): Round = x
\begin{Fortress}
\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
